title: webhook SSRF public-IP check: classify IPv6-transition addresses by their embedded IPv4, never by bare ip.is_global
answers: Webhook registration rejects a URL whose hostname resolves to an IPv6 address like 64:ff9b::169.254.169.254 or ::ffff:100.64.0.1, but the same IP was accepted before
Why does my HTTPS icon URL or other public URL validation reject an IPv4-mapped or 6to4 address?
Where is the webhook private-network / metadata-address blocking done at connection time?
Which check decides whether a resolved webhook peer IP counts as public?
body:
Path: Webhook destination checks for URLs that must point at public hosts. Pre-flight hostname resolution runs through mlflow/utils/validation.py:_validate_hostname_resolves_to_public_ips (used by webhook URL and public HTTPS URL validation, e.g. icon URLs). Connection-time peer validation runs through mlflow/webhooks/ssrf.py:_assert_public_peer on the socket's getpeername() address.
Rule: Both guards must decide public vs. non-public with mlflow/utils/validation.py:_is_public_ip, not a direct `ip.is_global`. _is_public_ip calls _embedded_ipv4, which unwraps IPv4-mapped (::ffff:0:0/96), 6to4 (`.sixtofour`), and NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96, low 32 bits) IPv6 addresses to the embedded IPv4 before checking is_global. If you add a new IP classification on these paths, route it through the same helper.
Symptom: A webhook or public URL pointing at cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) or a CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10) host, wrapped as NAT64, IPv4-mapped, or 6to4 IPv6, was accepted as a public destination, bypassing the earlier SSRF fix.
Constraints: Applies to the public-IP decision only. Plain IPv4 and genuinely public IPv6 (e.g. 2001:4860:4860::8888, ::ffff:8.8.8.8) must still pass. Private IPv4 is blocked as before. The helpers are underscore-named but imported across modules (validation.py -> webhooks/ssrf.py).
applies: Any code in MLflow that decides whether a webhook, icon, or other user-supplied URL/IP is a public address, both pre-resolution and at socket connect time.
says: Webhook registration permits destination links that tunnel to internal cloud metadata services.
Block webhook endpoints that reach private networks or metadata hosts through mapped addresses.
The custom icon URL field accepts addresses resolving to private cloud infrastructure.
Outgoing webhook connections must refuse requests directed at cloud metadata through mapped addresses.
